column1: # Applied symbol names for ps3-hdfury-eu EBOOT.elf (BCES-00664).
# The analysed file is the decrypted ELF, not the disc's EBOOT.BIN - see
# README.md. Addresses are the ELF's own virtual addresses: code lives at
# 0x00010000..0x00858e48 and data at 0x00860000, so a PS3 row is easy to tell
# from a PSP one (0x088xxxxx) or a PS2 one (0x002xxxxx) at a glance.
# `function` or `data`. The evidence lives in the page named in the last
# column; this file exists so the names can be re-applied to a fresh Ghidra
# database without hand-editing, and apply-ghidra-names.py refuses any row
# whose address and name do not both still appear on that page.
# Apply with the program open in a bridge-connected Ghidra:
#   scripts/apply-ghidra-names.py            # every binary, this one included
# opportunistic - this is not a milestone target, see README.md.
